messages:
alex: Heads-up: proposing Terraform changes to our GPU spot pools to cut costs and make interruptions graceful. TL;DR: switch ASG to mixed_instances_policy with capacity_optimized allocation, add instance weighting, tighter launch_template tagging, and a lifecycle hook -> SQS -> lambda drain flow. Canary in us-west-2 gpu-pool-1. Details below, please review.

maria: ok. can you paste the TF diff or the snippet for the launch_template + mixed policy? want to review tags and instance selection.

alex: here’s the snippet I’m testing in staging (abridged):
```hcl
resource "aws_launch_template" "gpu" {
  name_prefix   = "redwood-gpu-"
  image_id      = var.gpu_ami_id
  instance_type = "p3.2xlarge" # default fallback
  user_data     = base64encode(templatefile("templates/gpu-bootstrap.sh", {}))

  tag_specifications {
    resource_type = "instance"
    tags = {
      "redwood:env" = var.env
      "redwood:team" = "ml-infra"
      "cost-center" = var.cost_center
    }
  }
}

resource "aws_autoscaling_group" "gpu_mixed" {
  name                      = "redwood-gpu-mixed-${var.env}"
  mixed_instances_policy {
    launch_template {
      launch_template_specification {
        launch_template_id = aws_launch_template.gpu.id
        version            = "\$Latest"
      }
    }
    instances_distribution {
      on_demand_percentage_above_base_capacity = 10 # small on-demand buffer
      spot_allocation_strategy                 = "capacity-optimized"
    }
    override { instance_type = "p4d.8xlarge"  weighted_capacity = "16" }
    override { instance_type = "g5.2xlarge"  weighted_capacity = "4" }
    override { instance_type = "p3.2xlarge"  weighted_capacity = "8" }
  }

  min_size = var.min
  max_size = var.max
  tags = [
    { key = "Name", value = "redwood-gpu", propagate_at_launch = true },
    { key = "redwood:pool", value = var.pool, propagate_at_launch = true }
  ]

  lifecycle { create_before_destroy = true }
}
```

jin: couple questions:
- are we constraining AMI/arch so we don’t accidentally pick a non-x86 AMI for some instance types?
- how do we ensure GPU drivers / container runtime work across p3/p4/g5?

alex: good catches. plan is:
- AMI is baked and matched against an allowed_amis map by instance family (we already have P3/P4/G5 AMIs). TF selects image_id via a lookup: var.allowed_amis[substr(instance_type,0,2)] fallback to var.default_ami. prevents random cross-arch.
- user_data is minimal; AMIs have GPU drivers + nvidia-container-runtime preinstalled. For any new instance family we update the ami pipeline and rotate.
- we’ll add a node label and taint on launch_template user_data so kubelets report node.kubernetes.io/gpu-type=p3|p4 and scheduling can prefer correct pods.

ops-ryan: on interruptions: are we using lifecycle hook + SQS for the spot termination notice? We’ve seen TTLs spike when drain takes too long. Need graceful eviction to avoid hitting pod disruption budgets.

alex: yes: lifecycle hook on ASG -> send to SQS (with instance-id + lifecycle-action-token). Lambda picks it up, calls `kubectl drain --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data --force` against the node, then completes the lifecycle action. Also:
- we’ll run a small pre-stop sanity script on the node for checkpointing long-running jobs (e.g., copy checkpoint to S3).
- kube-proxy and CNI cleanup delay set to 10s to speed teardown.
- we have a fallback that if drain fails within 90s we mark the node NotReady and complete lifecycle so autoscaling can replace it.

maria: will that play nicely with cluster-autoscaler? draining + lifecycle delay can mean CA thinks capacity still exists and will not scale. We need a test plan.

alex: agree. rollout plan:
1) staging: apply TF changes to staging ASG (gpu-staging-pool) with min=0 max=2, monitor: node join time, drain latency, pod eviction success, interruption-to-replace time.
2) canary prod: target 1 ASG in us-west-2, enable `on_demand_percentage_above_base_capacity = 10` and `spot_allocation_strategy = capacity-optimized`, set ASG min to current baseline and drain hook enabled. Run for 48h.
3) metrics to watch: spot_interruption_rate, avg drain_time, pod PDB violations, GPU_utilization, and cost/GPU-hour.
4) if interruption_rate > 8% or PDB violations > 2% escalate and rollback: revert ASG to previous launch_template and disable mixed_instances_policy.

jin: also add automation to rotate AMI: we should tag AMI with `redwood:gpu-family=p4` etc, and a TF data source that selects latest non-expired image.

maria: for tags, let's standardize: `redwood:env`, `redwood:team`, `redwood:pool`, `cost-center`. Ops needs cost-center dimension for reporting.

ops-ryan: add alerting:
- fired when `spot_interruption_rate > 5% for 15m`
- `kube:pod_eviction_failures > 3 in 10m`
- `ASG:Desired != InService for > 3m`

sre-bot: rule created: alert/spot_interruption_rate_high (threshold=5% / 15m) -> notify #incidents and #eng-infra

deploy-bot: terraform plan finished for staging/gpu-staging-pool: 6 to add, 2 to change. See run: https://console.tf.example/runs/987654

maria: minor nit: make sure launch_template has `metadata_options { http_tokens = "required" }` and instance profile has least privilege for S3/GCS.

alex: yep added `metadata_options` and tightened IAM. Also added `propagate_at_launch = true` tags so billing is consistent.

ops-ryan: one more: ensure mixed instances weighting math is tested—some pods expect 8 GPUs per node assumed in scheduler. if g5 has 1 GPU vs p4d has 8, weight must reflect GPU capacity. Otherwise binpacking issues.

alex: using weighted_capacity to represent GPU count, and node labels `gpu.count` for scheduler extenders. will validate in staging.

maria: sweet. when you open the PR, tag me + jin. include the TF plan and the lambda drain runbook.

alex: will do. plan to open PR after staging validation (~tomorrow). thanks all :thumbsup:

sre-bot: note: created temp dashboard `gpu-spot-canary` for monitoring drain_time, interruption_rate, gpu_util, and asg_inservice_count.
